p: Paignton Zoo is big, and with so many animals and plants to see, it pays to grab a map and work out a route as soon as you arrive. Start with the animals your family is most excited about, as energy levels drop as the day goes on, and slot in keeper talks where you can. The lake area is a lovely spot to pause, and on a sunny day there's plenty of space for a picnic. With some steep sections, buggy pushers should be ready for a bit of a workout.

The zoo sits on the edge of Paignton, a short distance from the seafront, so it's easy to combine with the rest of the town. Goodrington Sands, just south, has a long sandy beach and Splashdown Quaywest waterpark nearby for warmer days. The Dartmouth Steam Railway runs from Paignton along the coast and down the Dart valley to Kingswear, where you can catch the ferry across to Dartmouth.

Back in town, Oldway Mansion, built for the Singer sewing machine family, is a grand building with gardens to explore. In Torquay, Kents Cavern is a network of prehistoric caves where people lived thousands of years ago, and guided tours make it a fascinating adventure for kids and adults alike. Babbacombe Model Village, up on the cliffs above Torquay, is a quirky miniature world that's great fun to explore. Brixham, with its working harbour and replica of the Golden Hind, rounds off a brilliant few days on the English Riviera.
